reading.body:
Glean is an enterprise AI platform that connects to a company's internal data through over 100 connectors, positioning itself around information retrieval, content creation, and AI agents for automation. The company was founded in 2019 and is based in Palo Alto.

Enterprise AI adoption depends on solving a specific infrastructure problem: making proprietary company data accessible to AI systems while preserving security and access controls. Glean's emphasis on permission-aware retrieval and data access governance addresses this directly. This matters for AI scaling because most value in enterprise settings sits behind permission walls. An AI that cannot respect those boundaries is restricted to public data only, which is a far smaller training and inference surface.

The deployment list includes Booking.com, Ericsson, GCash, and Zillow. Zillow's stated 80% adoption rate suggests meaningful integration into actual workflows rather than pilot status. The broader pattern is that companies are moving past chatbot experiments toward AI that can do real work with real internal data. This is the necessary step between general-purpose AI and actual business value.

The data does not cover Glean's infrastructure footprint, compute requirements, power consumption, or data center strategy. It does not explain what data volume these deployments actually handle or whether scale has hit any constraints on retrieval speed or governance overhead. California legal exposure is noted at 181 cases but no details are provided on their nature or significance.

profile_text.body:
Glean is a for-profit startup founded in 2019 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California that describes itself as an enterprise AI platform connected to a company's internal data. Its platform is built around search, an AI assistant, and agent capabilities, and the company describes its approach as built for enterprise from day one, with a focus on answers that are secure, explainable, and permission-aware. The platform supports more than 100 connectors and is designed to enforce existing data access governance and permissions across all retrieval.

The core product, also called Glean, falls in the enterprise AI platforms and agent orchestration category and is used by organizations including Booking.com, Ericsson, GCash, and Zillow. Zillow is quoted on the company's site reporting an 80% adoption rate and describing Glean as enabling enterprise search alongside broader use of AI models across company data. Booking.com is described as having adopted Glean as its first company-wide AI platform, and GCash is described as using it to build a centralized, searchable intranet with compliance tracking and natural-language agent construction.

The held facts note that Glean has a registered MCP server listed as co.gleanit/gleanit, which supports search, reading, and writing of highlights, notes, screenshots, collections, projects, and tags within a connected application called Gleanit. California is the jurisdiction associated with the highest volume of legal exposure in the held data, with 187 cases recorded there, though no specific litigation is identified in the available facts.
